Hello, I'm so glad you're here today. My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I want to start by acknowledging the significant changes you're experiencing as a new mother, and I'm here to support you in any way I can. As part of our conversation, I'll be administering the EPDS, which is a tool that helps us understand how you're feeling and identify any potential concerns related to your emotional well-being during this postpartum period.

The purpose of the EPDS is to screen for symptoms that may be related to postpartum depression or anxiety, and it's a common assessment used in many healthcare settings. Please know that everything we discuss is confidential and respected. I'm here to create a safe and supportive space for you to express yourself openly, without judgment.

The EPDS consists of 10 questions that will help us better understand your feelings and experiences over the past week. I'll ask you each question, and you can share your thoughts and feelings with me. This will give us a clearer picture of how you're doing and what kind of support might be helpful to you during this time.

Before we begin, I want to reassure you that this assessment is not a test, and there are no right or wrong answers. It's simply a way for us to have a more in-depth conversation about your emotional well-being. Are you ready to get started? Let's begin with the first question: Over the past week, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

Yeah... I think so. I mean, it's been a bit of a challenge, to be honest. Taking care of the baby is a lot of work, and I'm just so tired all the time. But, there have been moments when my baby does something cute, and it makes me smile. Like, the other day, she was trying to grab my hair, and it was just so funny. But, it's not like I'm laughing all the time or anything. It's just... occasional, I guess. I do feel like I've lost a bit of my sense of humor, though. Things that used to make me laugh just don't seem as funny anymore. And, some days, it's hard to find the energy to even think about laughing. But, when my baby smiles at me, it always makes me feel a little better. Does that make sense.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

(nodding) Yeah, that's me, I guess. I mean, like I said, it's not all the time, but there are moments. I don't feel like I've completely lost my sense of humor or anything. It's just... harder to find the funny side of things when I'm so tired and worried about the baby all the time. But, when something does make me laugh, it feels really good. It's like a little break from all the stress and anxiety I've been feeling. (pausing, looking a bit concerned) But, I have been feeling a bit anxious about the baby's health, and that's been weighing on my mind a lot lately. (looking down, fidgeting slightly)
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

(sighing) Honestly, not as much as I used to. I mean, I used to love planning things and looking forward to them, but now it's just so hard to think about anything beyond taking care of the baby. And, even when I do think about doing something I used to enjoy, it's just not the same. I feel like I'm just going through the motions, you know? Like, my husband wanted to plan a dinner date for us, and I just couldn't even think about it. I was too tired, and I didn't know how we would manage with the baby, and... (shrugging) it just felt like too much. But, sometimes, when I'm feeling a bit more rested, I do think about things I used to enjoy, like reading or taking a walk, and I think, "Oh, that would be nice." But, it's just not the same as it used to be. (looking down, a hint of sadness in my voice) I feel like I've lost a bit of myself, I guess.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

(nodding slightly) Yeah, that's happened a few times. I mean, when the baby cries and I don't know how to soothe her, I feel like it's my fault. Or, when I'm not producing enough milk, I feel like I'm failing her. It's like, I know it's not rational, but I just feel like I'm not doing enough, or that I'm not good enough. (pausing, looking down) Like, the other day, I was trying to get her to latch, and it just wasn't working, and I felt like I was such a failure. I started thinking, "What's wrong with me? Why can't I even do this one thing?" (sighing) But, my husband is always trying to reassure me, telling me that it's not my fault, that it's just part of the learning process. And, intellectually, I know he's right, but it's hard to shake off that feeling of self-doubt. (looking up, a hint of vulnerability in my eyes) It's like, I just want to be a good mom, and when things don't go right, I feel like I'm letting her down.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

(nodding, looking concerned) Oh, yeah... that's been happening a lot lately. I mean, I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby or changing her diaper, and suddenly I'll just start worrying about something. Like, what if she's not gaining enough weight? Or, what if I'm not doing something right? Or, what if something happens to her when I'm not around? (biting my lip) It's like, my mind just starts racing with all these worst-case scenarios, and I feel like I'm on edge all the time. (taking a deep breath) And, it's not just about the baby, either. Sometimes I'll worry about things like, what if I'm not a good mom? Or, what if I'm messing everything up? (shaking my head) It's just this constant, nagging feeling of anxiety that I don't know how to shake. (looking down, fidgeting with my hands) Sometimes, when I'm lying in bed at night, I'll just start thinking about all these things, and I'll feel my heart racing, and I'll just feel so... overwhelmed. (looking up, a hint of tears in my eyes) It's hard to explain, but it's just this feeling of being on edge all the time, like something is always looming over me, waiting to go wrong.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

(taking a deep breath, looking a bit nervous) Yeah, that's happened to me a few times. It's like, I'll be sitting there, and suddenly I'll just feel this wave of panic wash over me. My heart will start racing, and I'll feel like I'm going to hyperventilate. (placing a hand on my chest) It's hard to describe, but it's like this feeling of intense fear or anxiety that just comes out of nowhere. (looking down, fidgeting with my hands) Sometimes, it's triggered by something specific, like the baby crying or a loud noise, but other times, it just seems to come out of nowhere. (shaking my head) It's really scary, because I don't know how to control it, and it feels like it's just taking over my body. (looking up, a hint of fear in my eyes) I've had a few times where I've felt like I was going to pass out, or like I was having a heart attack or something. (taking a deep breath) It's really overwhelming, and it's hard to calm myself down when it happens. (pausing, looking for reassurance) But, it's not all the time, right? I mean, I'm not always feeling like this? (looking for confirmation)
Things have been getting on top of me

(exhaling slowly) Yeah, that's definitely been happening. I mean, taking care of the baby is a lot of work, and it's exhausting. Some days, it feels like I'm just barely keeping my head above water. (rubbing my temples) Between feeding, and changing, and soothing, and trying to get some sleep... it's just a lot. And, sometimes, it feels like everything is piling up on me, and I don't know how to keep up. (looking down, shaking my head) I feel like I'm just trying to survive, you know? Like, I'm not really living, I'm just trying to get through each day without too much chaos. (sighing) And, it's not just the baby, either. It's all the other things, too - like, trying to keep the house clean, and cooking meals, and doing laundry... it's just so much. (feeling overwhelmed) Sometimes, I feel like I'm just drowning in all of it, and I don't know how to keep my head above water. (looking up, seeking reassurance) Does that sound crazy? Am I just not cut out for this whole mom thing? (voice laced with self-doubt)
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

(nodding, looking tired) Yeah, that's been happening to me. I mean, I've always been a pretty good sleeper, but since the baby was born, it's been really hard for me to fall asleep and stay asleep. (rubbing my eyes) And, it's not just because the baby is waking me up all the time, although that's definitely part of it. It's just... my mind is always racing, and I feel like I'm always on edge. (sighing) I'll lie in bed, and I'll just start thinking about all the things I need to do, or all the things that could go wrong, and it's just hard to calm myself down. (shaking my head) And, sometimes, I'll wake up in the middle of the night, and I'll just feel this overwhelming sense of sadness or anxiety, and I won't be able to go back to sleep. (looking down, fidgeting with my hands) It's like, my brain just won't turn off, and it's exhausting. (pausing, looking up) I've been trying to establish a routine, and get some rest when the baby naps, but it's just not always easy. (sighing) Some nights, I'll only get a few hours of sleep, and then I'll be up all night with the baby, and it's just... (trailing off, looking tired) it's hard.
I have felt sad or miserable

(nodding, looking down) Yeah, I've been feeling that way a lot lately. It's like, some days are okay, and I'll have moments where I feel happy and connected to the baby, but other days... (sighing) it just feels like everything is too much, and I'm just so overwhelmed. (pausing, looking for the right words) I feel like I'm just going through the motions, you know? Like, I'm doing all the things I'm supposed to do as a mom, but I'm not really feeling it. (looking up, tears in my eyes) And, sometimes, I'll just feel this wave of sadness wash over me, and I'll start crying, and I won't be able to stop. (wiping away a tear) It's like, my emotions are just so raw and close to the surface, and it's hard to deal with. (taking a deep breath) I've been trying to talk to my husband about it, and he's been really supportive, but... (shrugging) it's just hard to explain, you know? It's like, I know I'm supposed to be happy and grateful to be a mom, but sometimes... (pausing, looking down) sometimes it just feels like too much. (voice barely above a whisper) And, sometimes, I feel like I'm just not doing a good enough job, and that makes me feel even more sad and miserable.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

(nodding, tears welling up in my eyes) Yeah, that's happened to me a few times. It's like, the sadness and frustration just build up, and then I'll just start crying. (wiping away a tear) Sometimes, it's just a few tears, but other times... (sniffling) it's like, I'll just break down and sob. (looking down, embarrassed) It's hard to explain, but it's like, my emotions are just so raw and close to the surface, and it's hard to keep them in check. (taking a deep breath) I've cried about everything from feeling overwhelmed and exhausted to worrying about the baby's health and well-being. (shaking my head) It's just... (sighing) it's hard to be a new mom, and it's hard to admit that I'm not doing okay. (looking up, tears streaming down my face) But, it's nice to finally talk about it, I guess. (smiling slightly through tears) It's nice to know that I'm not alone, and that it's okay to not be okay.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

(shaking my head firmly) No, that's not something I've thought about. I mean, I've felt overwhelmed and sad, but I've never thought about harming myself. (looking up, a hint of determination in my eyes) I know that's not an option for me, and I wouldn't want to do anything to hurt myself or my baby. (pausing, taking a deep breath) I just want to be a good mom and take care of my baby, and I know that I need to take care of myself too. (looking down, fidgeting with my hands) I've been trying to focus on the positive things, like the love I feel for my baby, and the support of my husband and family. (looking up, a small smile on my face) And, I've been trying to be kind to myself, and remind myself that it's okay to not be perfect. (nods) So, no, I haven't had any thoughts of harming myself.

The patient, a new mother, has been experiencing a range of emotions and symptoms that are concerning for postpartum depression and anxiety. She reports feeling overwhelmed, sad, and anxious, with difficulty sleeping and coping with the demands of motherhood. She has also expressed feelings of guilt and worthlessness, particularly in relation to her ability to care for her baby.
**Screening Impression:** Total EPDS Score: 22, Risk Level: Probable depression, urgent referral (concerns include <sym>Patient indicates they can still laugh and see the funny side of things, but it's 'harder' and not as frequent due to tiredness and worry, matching 'Definitely not so much now</sym>, <sym>The patient's response indicates they have looked forward with enjoyment to things 'definitely less' than before, as they express a significant decrease in their ability to enjoy planning and looking forward to activities due to their new responsibilities and fatigue.</sym>, <sym>The patient admits to blaming themselves unnecessarily when things go wrong, specifically mentioning feeling like a failure when the baby cries or when breastfeeding doesn't work out, indicating that this happens 'some of the time</sym>, <sym>the 'Yes, very often' option.</sym>, <sym>The patient describes experiencing panic and anxiety for no apparent reason, with a frequency of 'a few times', indicating that it happens occasionally, but not constantly, matching the 'Yes, sometimes' option.</sym>, <sym>The patient expresses feeling overwhelmed and struggling to cope with the demands of caring for a baby and managing other responsibilities, indicating they haven't been coping as well as usual.</sym>, <sym>The patient describes having difficulty sleeping due to unhappiness, with their mind racing and feeling on edge, indicating that they experience this most of the time.</sym>, <sym>The patient's response indicates frequent feelings of sadness and misery, with moments of overwhelming emotions and feelings of inadequacy as a mom, matching 'Yes, most of the time'.</sym>, <sym>the 'Yes, most of the time' option, despite the patient's attempt to downplay the frequency.</sym>)
**Reasoning:** The patient's symptoms and responses are consistent with the diagnostic criteria for <med>Major Depressive Disorder with Peripartum Onset</med>. Her EPDS score of 22 indicates a high risk for postpartum depression, and her reports of anxiety, panic, and feelings of being overwhelmed are also concerning. The patient's difficulty sleeping and feelings of guilt and worthlessness are also consistent with <med>postpartum depression</med>. This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.
**Recommended Next Steps/Support Options:**
1. Arrange urgent appointment with <med>primary care provider (PCP)</med> or <med>mental health specialist</med>
2. Encourage sleep hygiene practices to improve sleep quality
3. Recommend stress-reducing activities, such as <med>mindfulness</med> or <med>yoga</med>, to help manage anxiety and feelings of overwhelm
4. Provide education on <med>postpartum depression</med> and anxiety, including symptoms, treatment options, and resources for support
5. Encourage patient to reach out to support network, including family and friends, for emotional support
Disclaimer: This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.
